title: engine-plan.v1 — one immutable revision of a plan under deliberation, wrapping the exact Build payload
description: The plan document the Plan Coordinator mints, revises, and eventually seals. It is JSON and only JSON: there is no YAML working copy, no uncheckpointed-edit state, and no checkpoint verb — a revision is minted whole by `revise` and never edited in place, so the digest over its canonical form is the plan's identity. Two halves. The DELIBERATION half is the reasoning a Build cannot reconstruct: what problem this solves, the strongest case against doing it, the alternatives and why each was disposed of, how it could fail, and what remains undecided. The BUILD half is `build_plan` — the byte-exact payload the Build Coordinator will consume at `plan bind`, carried whole rather than re-derived, so a sealed plan and the Build it authorizes can never describe different work. NOTE ON `build_plan`, and please do not 'improve' it: it is deliberately typed as a bare object here with no properties, no required list, and no additionalProperties rule. Its authority belongs to the Build Coordinator, not to this schema — plan_contract.validate_document delegates to build_coordinator_dag.validate_plan_document, which applies the coordinator's own three layers (its schema for the declared version, work-item-id uniqueness, and DAG closure) against the same code path `plan bind` runs. Re-expressing any of those rules here would create a second notion of a valid payload that could drift from the first, and the drift would surface as a plan that seals cleanly and then fails at bind.

plan_id.description: Minted once at `init` and never reissued — not by revision, not by retitling, not by clone (a clone mints its own). The folder slug is a convenience for humans; this is the identity.

revision.description: Monotonic from 1. Revisions are immutable and every one is kept: the ledger is the record of how the plan got here, and a reader who only ever sees the head cannot tell a settled decision from a reversed one.

revision_note.description: What changed in this revision and why — written for the operator reading the ledger months later, not for the tool.

raw.description: What the operator actually said, kept verbatim. Never tidied, never paraphrased into the interpretation: the gap between the two is exactly what a reviewer needs to see.

case_against.description: The strongest honest argument for NOT doing this, stated at its full weight. A plan that cannot state one has not been deliberated; a decoy here is worse than an empty field, because it launders the absence of thought.

unresolved_decisions.description: Open questions the operator still owes an answer to. The array may be non-empty for as long as the plan is a draft; the seal refuses while any entry remains, which is the whole point of recording them.

operator_decisions.description: Decisions the operator made by name, kept so a later session cannot quietly re-litigate a settled call.

intake.description: Where this plan came from when it did not start here — an imported native Claude or Codex plan, or prose drafts that preceded it. Groundwork, not authority: an import lands as an unapproved draft with its gaps marked as gaps.

program.description: Optional linkage into a multi-PR program (engine-program.v1). Absent for a standalone plan, and absent is the normal case — a plan is per-Build, and a program is a deliberate act, never inferred from resemblance.

build_plan.description: The exact Build payload, carried whole. Intentionally unconstrained here — see the note in this schema's own description before adding any rule to this object.

intent_source.description: Mirrors build-plan.v2's own intent_source shape, because an unattended (Routine) Build still draws its AUTHORIZATION from a durable Issue even once the plan authority is local.

carried_obligation.description: An obligation handed forward from a predecessor plan. `released` is the escape hatch and it costs a stated reason — the guarantee is not that obligations are always met, only that one can never be dropped silently.
